title: Stephen Curry Chooses Flexibility Over a Max Deal
htmlContent:
Stephen Curry has never played for any team other than the Golden State Warriors, and now it looks like he never will. The four-time champion has agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension that runs through his 20th NBA season, according to ESPN's Shams Charania. The final year, 2028–29, is a player option.

The headline number is enormous, but the more telling detail is the money Curry left on the table. He was eligible for up to $136.7 million over two years. Instead, he took roughly $20 million less, and he did it to give the Warriors something they have lacked for years: room to maneuver.

Three Paths, One Decision

Curry became eligible for an extension on Aug. 29 while playing on an expiring $62.6 million contract. Over the following weeks, the Warriors walked him through his options. He could sign for the full max, accept a modest pay cut, or wait and let the season play out before committing to anything.

Each path came with trade-offs. The max offered the most money. Waiting offered more information about the roster and his own health. The pay cut offered security for Curry and financial breathing room for the franchise. After nearly a month of weighing it, Currychose the third option, and he did so three days before the team's first practice.

That timing mattered to him. Curry had made clear he wanted his contract settled without distraction before training camp, and by signing when he did, he removed the biggest storyline hanging over the start of Golden State's season.

How the Numbers Break Down

Curry's salary will actually decline before it rises again. After earning $62.6 million this season, he will make $55.7 million in 2027–28, followed by a $60.2 million player option in 2028–29.

That dip in 2027–28 is the whole point. According to team sources, the structure frees up about $10 million in additional projected cap space next summer, giving Golden State more firepower in free agency or on the trade market over the next year.

The Warriors' books are already set to change dramatically. Jimmy ButlerIII's $56.8 million contract and Draymond Green's $27.6 million deal both expire next summer. Kristaps Porzingis has just $3 million of his $20 million salary guaranteed. ESPN's Bobby Marks projects Golden State could have anywhere from $38 million to $55 million in cap space, depending largely on how it handles Brandin Podziemski, who has not yet signed an extension and carries a $17 million cap hold.

Why Curry Took Less

Curry was open about his thinking in the days leading up to the deal. Speaking with ESPN earlier in the week, he said his priority was playing on a competitive team and giving the front office the flexibility it had been missing in recent seasons. He described the situation as unusual, shaped by where the franchise has been over the last four years, where he is in his career, and what he called the team's "absolute desperation to win."

For a player who has already collected four championships and two MVP awards, the calculation was less about another payday and more about maximizing the window he has left. A few million dollars less per year could be the difference between Golden State standing pat and landing another impact player next summer.

Health and the Road Ahead

The biggest question surrounding Curry is not his shooting, which remains elite, but his body. He turns 39 this season and missed 39 games last year with a lingering right knee issue.

Curry insists that is behind him. He said he used the offseason well, feels great physically, and enters camp without any hesitation about where he stands. He also said he is simply excited to get back to work.

Golden State will need that version of Curry. The Warriors are built around the idea that he can still carry an offense deep into the spring, and this contract is a bet that he can do it for at least two more seasons.

A Historic Milestone

The extension also puts Curry in territory no NBA player has reached. With this deal, his career on-court earnings climb to $652 million, making him the first player in league history to surpass $600 million.

It is a fitting number for a player who reshaped how the game is played. But the way he reached it may say even more about him. At the point in his career when many stars would lock in every possible dollar, Curry chose to give some of it back in exchange for a better shot at one more title.
excerpt: Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors through his 20th NBA season, leaving roughly $20 million on the table to give the franchise financial flexibility to pursue additional impact players.
